derived_from.operation: generate a redesigned Suzaku concept with explicitly repeated modular stone, wood, rail, cloud, and mountain vocabulary for an 8x8 tile-economy experiment.

purpose: New tile-conscious panorama concept for offline conversion and comparison; not native Mega Drive art or approved production art.
prompt: Create a revised, tile-conscious production-art concept for this Mega Drive fighting-game stage. Preserve the recognizable composition: centered Japanese castle beneath a large full moon, layered night mountains and clouds, a long fighting platform with a wooden guardrail, two lanterns near the sides. Keep the same very wide panoramic 640x224 framing and horizon/layout if possible. This is an image concept to be translated into Genesis VDP art, not a finished game screenshot: no fighters, HUD, text, logos, gradients, blur, photorealism, or fake scanlines. Design for exact 8x8 tile reuse: the stone wall should use a small family of visibly coherent repeating 8x8 masonry motifs; the wood floor should use a small repeatable board/rivet vocabulary; rail posts should repeat at regular intervals; mountain/cloud silhouettes should be broad, clean clusters. Limit fine-grain texture and tiny random highlights. Make the castle silhouette and moon the strongest focal points, keep the playable floor flat and uninterrupted across the full width, and keep visual contrast high enough for foreground fighters. Use restrained deep navy, cool blue, stone lavender, warm wood brown, and small amber lantern accents; crisp 16-bit arcade background concept with deliberate clusters and no dithering noise. Aim for a polished, authored 1990s console fighting-game stage while reducing unique tile variation through intentional modular design.
